sulfurCube.title: Sulfur cube launch mechanics
sulfurCube.scope: Java Edition 26.2 · Bouncy archetype · one ordinary direct non-projectile knockback call · cube initially at rest
sulfurCube.assumptions.title: Scope and fixed assumptions
sulfurCube.assumptions.intro: This first milestone keeps the following assumptions fixed:
sulfurCube.assumptions.call: The attack makes one ordinary damage knockback call with effect factor E = 1.
sulfurCube.assumptions.cube: The adult Bouncy sulfur cube starts at rest and uses its JE 26.2 dimensions and properties. The experiment presets place its feet at (0, 0, 0).
sulfurCube.assumptions.aim: The aim point constructs the attacker's look direction; it is not a sampled collision point.
sulfurCube.assumptions.trajectory: The trajectory is an illustrative free-flight continuation without collisions, bouncing, fluids, or later attacks.
sulfurCube.invalidInputs: Enter finite numbers, use a whole-number trajectory horizon from 0 to 200 ticks, and keep the aim point distinct from the eye position.
sulfurCube.controls.title: Inputs
sulfurCube.controls.presetHelp: M1–M9 are recorded direct-melee experiment fixtures used to check distinct aim, elevation, and damage cases.
sulfurCube.controls.damageArgumentHelp: The nonnegative damage value passed to this knockback call; this is not necessarily health lost.
sulfurCube.controls.coordinatesHelp: Use these fields as an alternative to the scene handles or to edit lateral X/Z coordinates outside the radial view.
sulfurCube.controls.cubeFeetHelp: World coordinates of the bottom center of the sulfur cube.
sulfurCube.controls.attackerFeetHelp: World coordinates used for the cube-to-attacker elevation calculation and horizontal base direction.
sulfurCube.controls.attackerEyesHelp: World coordinates supplied independently from the feet position. The presets use the standing-player eye height of 1.62 blocks.
sulfurCube.controls.aimPointHelp: Defines look direction from the eye position. It does not represent where the attack collided with the cube.
sulfurCube.controls.trajectoryTicksHelp: A whole number from 0 to 200 ticks. The default M1 view ends about two blocks below the starting cube center; this does not simulate collisions or bounces.
sulfurCube.scene.svgDescription: A pannable and zoomable radial side view showing the sulfur cube, the standing player's hitbox, feet and eyes, a fixed-length look arrow, launch velocity, and the first part of the calculated free-flight trajectory.
sulfurCube.scene.aimHandleAria: Move aim point, currently x {x}, y {y}, z {z}. Use arrow keys for small steps and Shift plus an arrow key for larger steps.
sulfurCube.scene.attackerHandleAria: Move the attacker while preserving eye height and look direction. Use arrow keys for small steps and Shift plus an arrow key for larger steps.
sulfurCube.scene.cubeHandleAria: Move the sulfur cube by its center handle. Use arrow keys for small steps and Shift plus an arrow key for larger steps.
sulfurCube.scene.interactionHelp: Drag an object handle to move only that input, drag the empty background to pan, and scroll over the scene or use −/+ to zoom. Arrow keys move a focused handle by 0.05 blocks; hold Shift for 0.25-block steps.
sulfurCube.scene.projectionHelp: This side-view plane is initially aligned along the cube-to-attacker horizontal axis and stays fixed while objects move. Lateral X/Z values remain part of the 3D calculation and can be edited in the coordinate fields, even though they are not visible in this plane.
sulfurCube.scene.trajectoryTruncated: The scene shows the first {shown} of {requested} requested ticks to keep the launch geometry readable; the detailed result still evaluates the full horizon.
sulfurCube.power.title: How aim and height determine launch power
sulfurCube.power.subtitle: Internal horizontal/vertical power space—not world-space velocity.
sulfurCube.power.svgDescription: A diagram showing the Bouncy base power, vertical aim transfer, feet-elevation rotation, and component-ratio cap inside the horizontal and vertical power axes.
sulfurCube.power.stages.baseHelp: The Bouncy archetype's starting horizontal and vertical powers.
sulfurCube.power.stages.aimHelp: Vertical aim redistributes power between the two components using q.
sulfurCube.power.stages.elevationHelp: Relative attacker-feet elevation rotates the pair using θ.
sulfurCube.power.stages.cappedHelp: The pair is scaled together when either archetype-relative component exceeds its limit.
sulfurCube.power.capApplied: The component cap is active here: the rotated pair is multiplied by {factor} to reach the final internal power.
sulfurCube.power.capNotApplied: The rotated pair is already within both component limits, so the cap does not rescale it.
sulfurCube.power.capExplanation: The dashed rectangle represents separate horizontal and vertical component ratios. It is not a circular limit on Euclidean vector length.
sulfurCube.readout.title: Calculated launch
sulfurCube.readout.finalPosition: Cube feet position after horizon (x, y, z)
sulfurCube.readout.provenanceBehavior: Knockback behavior is derived from locally decompiled Java Edition 26.2 code.
sulfurCube.readout.provenanceData: Bouncy properties and sulfur cube dimensions are derived from Java Edition 26.2 data and runtime initialization.
sulfurCube.readout.standardMath: This version uses standard TypeScript number and trigonometric operations; source-precision emulation is planned separately.
